summary: Daughter of the Palatine-German Croup family of Nanticoke and Hunlock's Creek (about 1802–1895), wife of James Pringle of Plymouth; John's 4th-great-grandmother.
bio:
Elizabeth Croup, whose family name was also written Grub and Croop, was born about 1802, probably in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania. Her parents, Frederick Croup and Mary Young, had moved there from Forks Twp in Northampton County about 1799 or 1800, when her sister Susan was born at Nanticoke in May 1800; the Croups were a Palatine-German family settled at Hunlock's Creek and Nanticoke. Her brothers and sisters were Susan, John, Peter, Mary, Margaret, Catherine, Ann and William. Her father died in 1841, leaving a will as a resident of Plymouth Twp.

She married James Pringle and had at least five children with him, among them John's ancestor Andrew G. Pringle. In August 1860, aged 57, she was living on the family farm in Plymouth with James and their youngest son Edwin, with Andrew next door. By July 1870 James was living with Andrew and Elizabeth was no longer in the household. Family records say she died in 1895 in Indiana, which would fit her having gone west with relatives, as her niece Mary (Shupp) Nesbitt had done when she moved to Rolling Prairie, Indiana, in 1853; it is also possible that she died in the 1860s. She is John's 4th-great-grandmother.

researchNotes:
Elizabeth Croup was born about 1802 (1850 census age 48; tree 1802-1895), probably in Luzerne County, where her family had moved from Forks Twp, Northampton County, about 1799-1800 (her sister Susan was born at Nanticoke in May 1800). Her parents were Frederick Croup/Grub and Mary Young. She married James Pringle and had at least five children, including John's ancestor Andrew G. Pringle. FamilySearch lists her siblings as Susan (1800), John, Peter, Mary, Margaret, Catherine, Ann and William. She died in 1895 (tree; unsourced).

Elizabeth was alive in August 1860, aged 57, on the family farm in Plymouth with her husband James and youngest son Edwin; her son Andrew lived next door ([R4-S1]). By July 1870 James was living with Andrew and she was not in the household ([R4-S2]). Either she had died in the 1860s, or she was living elsewhere - the tree's death in 1895 'IN' (Indiana?) is unsourced, but would fit her going west with relatives (her niece Mary (Shupp) Nesbitt went to Rolling Prairie, Indiana, in 1853). Her father's will is indexed as 'Croup, Frederick, Plymouth Twp., 1841, Will Book B p.80' in the Luzerne County wills index ([R4-S3]); it should name her as Elizabeth Pringle.
